title: A friendly wrong-number text

segments.text: Hi David, are we still meeting at the tennis club at three?
Oh sorry, wrong number! You seem very kind though, my name is Linda.

flag.reason: Scammers pretend to text the wrong person on purpose to start a casual conversation.

segments.text: Do you live around here? I love chatting with new friends online.

flag.reason: They try to build trust over days or weeks before asking for money or pitching fake investments.

explanation: Wrong-number scams start with a polite text to get you talking. Once a connection is made, the stranger turns to money, sob stories, or fake investments. Never reply to strangers who text you by mistake.
takeaways: Do not reply to texts from strangers.
Block and delete unexpected friendly messages.

title: Online acquaintance pitching a secret investment

segments.text: Good morning! It has been so lovely chatting with you this past week.
My uncle who works as a chief investment director showed me a private trading portal with guaranteed 15% daily returns.

flag.reason: There is no such thing as a guaranteed high return with zero risk. Promises of guaranteed profits are always fraudulent.

segments.text: I already withdrew $6,000 this morning! I can guide you if you send $500 to my special wallet link today.

flag.reason: The stranger built a friendly connection solely to steal your money through a counterfeit investment website.

segments.text: Let me know within the hour before the European markets close!

explanation: This is known as a relationship-investment scam. Criminals spend days acting as friendly pen pals before introducing a fraudulent crypto or trading platform. Never invest funds through links provided by strangers.
takeaways: Never invest money through websites recommended by strangers.
Any claim of guaranteed high returns is a scam.

title: Evaluating a work-from-home job offer
prompt: You receive a text offering a $45/hour work-from-home administrative job without an interview. Which response protects you?

options.label: Delete the text, because real companies do not hire strangers via random text messages
Accept the job, deposit the $2,500 check they mail you for home office equipment, and wire the leftover money back
options.note: They say the vendor needs immediate payment

reasons.a: Correct: Legitimate employers conduct formal interviews and do not send unsolicited job offers with high salaries via text message.
reasons.b: Dangerous: The check is counterfeit. Your bank will make funds available initially, but when the fake check bounces a week later, you must repay the bank every dollar you wired.

explanation: Fake check scams frequently disguise themselves as work-from-home job offers. When a counterfeit check bounces, the victim is held financially responsible by their bank for all withdrawn or wired money.
takeaways: Never deposit a check from an employer you never met in person.
Real employers send equipment directly, never money to wire.
